title: useSyncExternalStore: Concurrent Tearing Prevention in External Stores

progressiveExplaining.eli5: Imagine two painters drawing the same person. Painter 1 draws the top half. While Painter 2 starts the bottom half, the person suddenly changes their shirt. If the painters don't coordinate, the final picture has a blue shirt on top and a red shirt on the bottom (visual tearing). `useSyncExternalStore` forces React to pause and synchronize so every part of the screen sees the exact same shirt.
progressiveExplaining.junior: `useSyncExternalStore` is the official hook for subscribing to non-React state stores (like Redux, Zustand, browser APIs like `window.navigator.onLine`, or custom event emitters). `const state = useSyncExternalStore(subscribe, getSnapshot, getServerSnapshot)`. It replaces `useEffect` + `useState` store subscriptions and guarantees that components never display inconsistent or torn state during concurrent rendering.
progressiveExplaining.senior: Architecturally, **Visual Tearing** occurs in React Concurrent Mode when a non-React mutable store mutates in the middle of an asynchronous, time-sliced render pass. If Component A reads version 1, the main thread yields to a store mutation (version 2), and Component B reads version 2 within the same render cycle, the committed UI becomes inconsistent. `useSyncExternalStore` detects store mutations during render and forces React to synchronously re-evaluate the tree, guaranteeing strict linear consistency.
progressiveExplaining.underTheHood: During the render phase, React invokes `getSnapshot()` and stores the snapshot on the fiber. Before committing the workInProgress tree, React calls `getSnapshot()` again. If the return value has changed (via `Object.is`), React detects a concurrent store mutation, bails out of the concurrent pass, and immediately restarts the render synchronously (`renderRootSync`) to prevent tearing.

interviewGotchas.question: Why must `getSnapshot` return an immutable cached value or primitive?
interviewGotchas.contextIntro: Interviewers test your knowledge of reference equality checks and infinite render loops.
interviewGotchas.detailedAnswer: React compares the return value of `getSnapshot()` using `Object.is`. If `getSnapshot` creates and returns a *new object or array reference on every call* (e.g. `() => ({ isOnline: navigator.onLine })`), React will believe the external store mutated on every single check, causing an **infinite re-render loop** and throwing a maximum update depth exceeded error.
interviewGotchas.trapWarning: Never return inline object literals `() => ({ ... })` from `getSnapshot`. Always return primitives or cached, immutable object references.

interviewGotchas.question: What is the purpose of the third parameter `getServerSnapshot`?
interviewGotchas.contextIntro: Checks understanding of Server-Side Rendering (SSR) hydration contracts.
interviewGotchas.detailedAnswer: `getServerSnapshot` is required when using Server-Side Rendering (SSR). During server generation and initial client hydration, React executes `getServerSnapshot` to ensure the rendered markup matches between server and client, preventing hydration mismatch errors for browser-specific globals like `window` or `navigator`.
interviewGotchas.trapWarning: If `getServerSnapshot` is omitted in an SSR app, calling `useSyncExternalStore` on the server will throw an error.
